subject: Re: Encord Evaluation
text:
Gents - many thanks for the convos earlier today.  As a follow up, I wanted
to share an easier to follow & digest set of requirements for our
workflow.  I don't believe we had the time to discuss one in particular -
presenting multiple sequential 1-hour recordings as a single continuous
video record: in other words, annotators should not have to concern
themselves with, or, ideally, even realize the fact that we have multiple
separate videos strung together.  Curious what the options are.  Tx!

navigation:

   - breakdown & stats by customer > facility > OR > date

continuous “day view” presentation:

   - our videos are recorded in 1-hour chunks (up to 13-14 separate files,
   200MB - 3+GB each), but are presented to the customer as a seamless,
   continuous day-long recording (by simply stringing separate files together…
   we also convert our videos to HLS to reduce playback latency)

multiple camera views: we have 1-8 cameras in a given OR, all recording,
generating separate sets of recorded videos

   - all available camera recordings are presented to the user at the same
   time via a grid, with one of the cameras selected for the larger “main view”
   - users can change which camera is in the “main view” at any time

playback:

   - synchronized playback / rewind / fforward for all camera views within
   the same "day" or "case" recording
   - speed controls - 1x - 30x

temporal segmentation:

   - segment the day into 1+ cases - by identifying case start & end for
   each case. this can be accomplished by identifying case boundaries in other
   ways - e.g., via events such as “case 1 start”, “case 1 end”, etc.

event timestamping:

   - each case is reviewed & timestamped for a fixed, predefined number of
   standard surgical events

annotation progress / coverage:

   - basic stats on annotation progress across the entire data set: by
   customer, etc.

assignment & work management:

   - assign / unassign video sets (in our context, we work with “days”) to

subject: Re: Encord Accelerate
text:
Hi Alex,

Perfect looking forward to it!

Regarding estimations,

We have at the moment:

1200 Chest CT:s that have aortas already labelled, but they need to be checked/finetuned and the landmarks would need to be placed. (shouldn't take much more than 10 min for these cases)

After this we have around 75000 CT:s(mainly chest) that we'll run our agents on first, but same thing there, finetuning/relabeling of the aorta, review and landmarks. Prob between 5-20min depending on the quality of our initial segmentation(should be pretty good by this point)

Then we have some other datasets as well between 2000-6000 images, of abdominal, chest and fullbody CT:s to be labelled, same thing as above. Overall as well the labeling of these projects makes sense to be split ( for example, 200 labelled initially, model trained, agent goes through rest, reviewing the rest)

In addition to these CT:s we also have a LOT of Ultrasound imaging that would need to be labelled, mainly of the carotid arteries. At the moment we have over 50 000 images there with no existing labels and expecting a lot more. These would only need to be labelled after most of the CT:s are done though.

Happy to discuss these things more in the call!

Thank you!

Best,
Onni
